title: SLA Credits
brief:
As a billing owner, I want outages measured against our SLA and credited on the invoice, so that customers are compensated when we miss the SLA.

Acceptance criteria:
- An outage longer than the SLA threshold earns a credit on the invoice; a shorter one earns none.
- The longer the outage, the higher the credit tier it reaches.
- The part of an outage that lies inside the billing period counts, even if the outage began before the period or ended after it.
- The SLA writes its durations the way people do, such as "30m" or "1h 30m".

steps.summary: Add the duration parser and the small time helpers it measures with
Add the SLA types: billing tiers, policy, outages and the invoice
Add the invoice generator that measures outages and credits the invoice
Add the tests and README section

items.question: An outage started 3 days before the billing period and ended 1 hour into it. What does the invoice credit for it (default policy)?
options: 5% of the subtotal, for the hour inside the period
Nothing: the outage is left out
25% of the subtotal, for the whole outage

items.question: Two outages of 20 minutes each fall into the same billing period (default policy, threshold "30m"). What does the invoice credit?
options: Nothing: each outage is measured on its own
5% of the subtotal: together they last 40 minutes
